Turkana moves to strengthen healthcare under BREHS project
items.description: Ministry of Health in collaboration with the World Bank and Turkana County Government has undertaken a five-day Implementation Support Mission for the Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems (BREHS) Project.
content: Ministry of Health in collaboration with the World Bank and Turkana County Government has undertaken a five-day Implementation Support Mission for the Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems (BREHS) Project.

The mission seeks to assess county preparedness, strengthen coordination among implementing partners and agree on priority actions to support effective project implementation, which aims to improve healthcare delivery for refugees and host communities.

According to a statement, the key areas include workforce and infrastructure readiness, risk management, implementation planning, financing and alignment with the Shirika Plan to improve healthcare delivery for refugees and host communities.
Turkana is among 45 counties that have met BREHS compliance requirements and qualified for the first tranche of project funding.

BREHS is a five-year initiative aimed at strengthening resilient health systems and expanding access to quality primary healthcare, particularly maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health services.
The Ministry remains committed to supporting county-led implementation, strengthening partnerships and ensuring equitable access to quality healthcare for all.

The Ministry’s delegation, led by BREHS Project Lead Dr Terry Kamau, was received by Turkana County CECM for Health and Sanitation Services Dr Epem Joseph, alongside Chief Officer for Medical Services Dr Gilchrist Lokoel and Chief Officer for Preventive and Promotive Health Services Agnes Mana.
The engagement brings together representatives from the Council of Governors, Public Service Commission, Kenya Medical Training College, County Health Management Team and other implementing partners.

The mission includes field assessments at Kakuma Health Facility and the proposed Lodwar blood service site, alongside discussions on KMTC sponsorship, infrastructure development, recruitment of technical personnel and resource utilisation.

World Bank Health Economist Paul Bartilol emphasised the need to begin preparations for FY2028 planning within the next three months to ensure county priorities are reflected in future funding allocations.
The mission will conclude with engagements involving the Governor and county leadership to review findings, agree on implementation milestones and strengthen county ownership.

items.title: Three More UDA Lawmakers Bolt to Gachagua's DCP as Transfer Window Nears Close
items.description: Three sitting Members of Parliament elected on the ruling United Democratic Alliance ticket have aligned with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua's…
content: Three sitting Members of Parliament elected on the ruling United Democratic Alliance ticket have aligned with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua's Democracy for the Citizens Party, bringing the outfit's claimed tally to 25 lawmakers.

Gachagua unveiled Gatundu South MP Gabriel Kagombe, Laikipia West MP Wachira Karani, and Nyeri Woman Representative Rahab Mukami at his Wamunyoro residence in Nyeri County on Tuesday morning, terming the move a defining moment for Mt Kenya politics.

"All politics is local. A defining moment for Mlima politics. Today, at my Wamunyoro residence, I welcomed three Members of Parliament, GG Kagombe, Wachira Karani, and Rahab Mukami, who have left UDA and joined the party of the moment and the future, DCP," Gachagua stated on his official X account.

The former deputy president urged other lawmakers still allied to President William Ruto's administration to abandon the ruling party and return to his political camp unconditionally before the end of the year.
"I welcome all leaders who wish to join our party and come back home unconditionally. Our transfer window is open to everyone and will close on 31st December 2026," Gachagua declared.

He expressed confidence that the wave of defections sweeping across the Mt Kenya region will dramatically expand his party's numerical strength in the National Assembly ahead of next year's general election.
"The DCP team has grown from 19 members to 25. I have no doubt that we will have 60 MPs by next year. The future is green. Green is wealth," he added.

Although the lawmakers have not yet formally written to the Registrar of Political Parties or the Speaker of the National Assembly to resign from UDA, they are expected to formalise their exit after February 10, 2027.

Under Kenyan electoral law, resigning from a sponsoring political party within six months of the August 10, 2027 general election no longer triggers costly parliamentary by-elections, giving defectors a safe legal window ahead of the March 16, 2027 party membership submission deadline.

For Kagombe, Tuesday's formal reception at Wamunyoro caps a turbulent political transition that began in August 2026, when the Gatundu South legislator first announced his exit from UDA during a tense public rally in his constituency.

At the time, hostile residents heckled Kagombe over his previous voting record in Parliament, prompting Gachagua to declare that the lawmaker would have to undergo strict party vetting and seek forgiveness from voters before being officially admitted into DCP.

The induction of Mukami, a close ally who previously backed President Ruto in Gachagua's home county of Nyeri, alongside Karani and Kagombe deals another blow to UDA's grassroots machinery in central Kenya.

The defections come barely four days after Runyenjes MP Eric Muchangi Karemba officially joined DCP at Wamunyoro last Friday, accelerating Gachagua's aggressive bid to consolidate Mt Kenya East and West ahead of 2027.

items.title: Karauri Fires Back at Gachagua Over Claims He Was Brought to Split Mt Kenya Votes in Nairobi
items.description: Kasarani Member of Parliament Ronald Karauri has hit back at former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua after the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader…
content: Kasarani Member of Parliament Ronald Karauri has hit back at former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua after the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader accused him of entering the Nairobi gubernatorial race to divide Mt Kenya votes in the capital.

In a statement on Monday, November 16, Karauri dismissed the allegations, maintaining that Nairobi residents were capable of independently choosing their preferred leaders ahead of the 2027 General Election.
The MP challenged Gachagua to stop blaming other political players whenever his political calculations failed to work out, insisting that Nairobi voters were not easily swayed by political influence.

"A bad dancer always blames the music, and when the music changes, they blame the dance floor. Dear Riggy G, why are you nervous? Don't always look for someone to blame whenever your political calculations don't add up," Karauri stated.
He further argued that Nairobi residents understood the challenges facing the city and would make independent decisions on who should lead them.
"Nairobi voters are not sheep waiting to be herded by whoever shouts the loudest. They are intelligent people who understand their city, their problems and the kind of leadership they deserve.
"They will decide who represents them, and as far as I am concerned, Nairobi has already found its Captain," he added.

Karauri's response followed remarks by Gachagua, who claimed that President William Ruto had facilitated the Kasarani MP's entry into the Nairobi gubernatorial contest to split support among Mt Kenya voters in the capital.
Speaking during a political engagement, Gachagua questioned whether residents from the Mt Kenya region would allow what he described as a political strategy to divide their votes.
"President Ruto has looked for Karauri and brought him to Nairobi so that he can divide the Mt Kenya votes; will you allow it?" Gachagua posed.

The exchange comes days after Karauri announced his decision to join the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), where he was received by National Assembly Majority Leader Kimani Ichung'wah and party Secretary General Hassan Omar.
In announcing his move, the legislator said he had settled on UDA after considering different political options as he prepares to contest the Nairobi gubernatorial seat in 2027.

"Today, I take a new political step by joining the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as I pursue my ambition to serve Nairobi as Governor in 2027. I looked at all the options and chose where I believe I can deliver for Nairobi," Karauri said.
The MP also expressed confidence in his ability to bring together Nairobi's diverse communities around a common development agenda.

His entry into the Nairobi gubernatorial race adds another dimension to the political contest for the county's top seat, with questions of party support, community voting patterns and competing political interests increasingly featuring in the campaigns ahead of the 2027 elections.

Several governments and local authorities across Europe, North America, and Asia are running financial incentive schemes designed to draw new residents, remote workers, and skilled professionals into areas struggling with population decline.

The programmes vary significantly in size and structure, but most share a critical limitation: the money does not come with a visa or immigration status. Applicants must typically already have the legal right to live and work in the country before they can qualify.

Ireland's Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant offers up to KSh 12 million (€84,000) to restore a derelict property on an offshore island or up to KSh 10 million (€70,000) for a derelict home on the mainland.

Applicants must own or be purchasing an eligible property that has been vacant for at least two years and was built before 2008. The renovated home must become the applicant's primary residence.
Portugal's Emprego Interior MAIS programme pays KSh 538,000 (€3,759.91) to workers who relocate to designated interior territories for permanent employment, self-employment, or business creation.
The base payment rises by 20% for each additional household member, plus KSh 115,300 (€805.70) towards removal costs. Third-country nationals with legal Portuguese residence are eligible.
Switzerland's Alpine village of Albinen in the canton of Valais offers KSh 3.87 million (CHF 25,000) per adult and KSh 1.55 million (CHF 10,000) per child.
A family of two adults and two children could collectively qualify for KSh 10.8 million (CHF 70,000).

Applicants must be under 45, purchase a qualifying primary home worth at least KSh 31 million (CHF 200,000), and commit to residing in the village for a minimum of 10 years. Foreign nationals must already hold a Swiss C residence permit.

Italy's Sardinian regional government provides grants of up to KSh 2.15 million (€15,000), capped at 50% of eligible costs, for the purchase or renovation of a first home in municipalities with populations below 5,000.

Japan's regional relocation programme offers up to KSh 816,500 (¥1 million) to households leaving the Tokyo metropolitan area, with the scheme primarily targeting people who have previously lived or worked in Tokyo.

In the United States, Ascend West Virginia pays selected remote workers KSh 1.56 million ($12,000) in monthly instalments over two years but limits eligibility to US citizens and lawful permanent residents.

Tulsa Remote in Oklahoma offers KSh 1.3 million ($10,000) to remote workers who relocate to the city; since 2018, more than 4,000 workers have participated. Both programmes require existing US work authorisation and do not sponsor visas.

Dubai Teaching Jobs for Foreigners: Qualifications Needed, Visas and Salaries You Can Expect
items.description: Dubai teaching jobs offer tax-free salaries up to AED 19,000, but Kenyan teachers must navigate KHDA permits, degree attestation costs and lengthy processing.
content: Dubai's private education sector remains one of the most financially attractive destinations for foreign teachers, with tax-free monthly salaries stretching from approximately AED 8,000 (roughly KSh 296,000) for newly qualified staff to more than AED 19,000 (approximately KSh 703,000) for experienced secondary school specialists.
Beyond the base pay, most contracts include furnished accommodation, annual return flights, and medical insurance.
The regulatory body governing private schools in the emirate, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA), sets the minimum qualifications for each teaching category.
High Commission of Canada in Kenya is hiring for trade position, offers KSh 3 million per year
Nursery teachers working with children aged 45 days to 35 months must hold a Level 3 QF Emirates qualification in early childhood education.
For all other roles, including pre-primary, primary, and secondary subject teaching, a Level 6 bachelor's degree is the floor.
Subject specialists teaching learners aged 6 to 18 must hold a degree relevant to their area, alongside at least one year of recent classroom experience or six months of supervised practice.
Every teacher in a Dubai private school must hold a KHDA teaching permit. Applications are submitted by the employing school, not the individual, through the KHDA Educator Management System.
The authority typically takes between 5 and 15 working days to review submissions.
Foreign qualifications must be attested by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the applicant's home country embassy in the UAE.
The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research must separately issue an equivalency certificate.
These attestation costs generally fall between AED 1,500 and AED 3,000, and the burden sits with the teacher. KHDA licensing fees, by contrast, are covered by the school.
German embassy invites Kenyans to apply for fully funded ITK course offering monthly grant
Permits are institution-specific. A teacher who changes schools must have the original permit cancelled and a fresh application submitted.
Those considering a mid-contract move should check notice period obligations carefully, as violations can trigger a 90-day delay before a new appointment notice is issued.

Schools must complete safer recruitment checks before hiring, including at least two professional references and police clearances from any country where the applicant has lived in the past five to ten years. Under Dubai's 2026 safeguarding framework, staff are barred from using personal devices, private contact details, or personal social media accounts to communicate with students; all contact must go through institutionally approved channels.

On pay, there is no KHDA-mandated salary scale. Packages vary by curriculum, with British and IB curriculum secondary maths teachers earning between AED 8,500 and AED 19,000 per month depending on experience, while primary teachers typically see salaries in the AED 12,600 to AED 13,800 range.

End-of-service gratuity is calculated on basic salary only: 21 days' basic pay for each of the first five years, then 30 days per year beyond that. A teacher on AED 10,000 basic who completes two years receives approximately AED 14,000. Kenyan applicants should verify that their contract places a reasonable portion of total compensation under "basic salary" rather than allowances, as the split directly affects gratuity.
Degree attestation and equivalency processing can take 8 to 12 weeks, so candidates planning a move should begin paperwork well in advance of their intended departure date

Betty Bayo’s Brother Responds to Claims that His Mum Travelled Back to Kenya from US
items.description: A viral TikTok falsely suggested Betty Bayo’s mother had returned to Kenya. Son Ngesh Daboprint responded, revealing tensions that remain after her death.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

A TikTok post claiming that Joyce Wairimu Mbugua, the mother of the late Betty Bayo, had returned to Kenya from the United States, sparked a flurry of reactions over the weekend before her son moved quickly to set the record straight.

The post, captioned "welcome back mama Betty Bayo," showed Joyce, commonly referred to as Mama Betty, smiling indoors in a red sequin dress while holding a bouquet of red roses and white baby's breath flowers.
Many fans who saw it took it as confirmation she had finally flown back home, more than a year after her daughter's passing.

Her son Ngesh Daboprint, whose real name is Edward Kang'ethe Mbugua, was having none of it.
Ngesh commented directly under the viral TikTok post, shooting down the idea that his mother was anywhere near Kenya. His words were blunt:
It is worth noting that the photo itself offers no proof of location. Joyce appears to be indoors in what looks like a home in Seattle, the US city where she is based.

There is no airport backdrop, no Kenyan family members visible, and no statement from Joyce herself confirming any travel. The image appears to have circulated previously, including in tributes shared following Betty's death.

Joyce, who is 76 years old, did not attend Betty's requiem mass or her burial at Mugumo Estate in Kiambu on 20th November 2025. She joined the ceremony remotely via video link and had a tribute read on her behalf.
Bayo, born Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, died in November 2025 at Kenyatta National Hospital after a battle with acute myeloid leukaemia, an aggressive form of blood cancer.

Shortly after the death, Joyce went live on social media alongside Shiru wa Oakland, calling for a post-mortem examination and urging Pastor Victor Kanyari, Bayo's ex-husband and father of her two children, to pursue custody through official channels.
Through lawyers, the family also petitioned the Director of Public Prosecutions in December 2025 for a formal inquest into Betty's death.
That inquest concluded in October 2026. Ngesh announced the closure on 1st October, writing:
We also highlighted facts about Bayo’s niece Glacia and her emotional message from the late gospel singer’s home on the first anniversary of her death.

Glacia said she had prayed, fasted and cried while caring for Bayo’s children, promising they would sing and pray through the night.
Her tribute came amid tensions between Bayo’s widower, Hiram Gitau, and her ex-husband, Pastor Victor Kanyari.

President William Ruto's son George Ruto had Kenyans in stitches over the weekend after dropping a cheeky comment on a viral video involving content creator Kennie Mutahi and his girlfriend Caroline.

The clip, which spread widely on social media on Saturday, November 14, showed Kennie showing up with flowers, chocolates and a white gift bag for Caroline following a prank that had left her visibly upset.
The bouquet came wrapped in black paper decorated with red hearts, and Caroline's expression softened as she received the gesture.

Rather than sulk, Kennie laughed it off, wrapped his arm around her shoulder, and lifted her up as the two shared a light-hearted moment together.
The clip quickly caught fire online, drawing reactions from thousands of Kenyans who found the whole sequence amusing.
Among those who could not resist commenting was George Ruto, who jumped into the conversation with a joke in Swahili .

Others were more sympathetic, pointing out that while thoughtful gifts are a good start after a disagreement, warming someone back up can take a little extra time and patience.

items.title: "Now we are stuck": Kenyan Prince's 2 cars sink at Diani Beach
items.description: Kenyan Prince’s Lamborghini Urus and Mercedes-Benz GLE became trapped in Diani Beach sand after a show-off drive, hours after he denied repossession rumours.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

Kenyan forex trader and social media personality Raymond Omosa, popularly known as Kenyan Prince, turned a fun coastal outing into an expensive headache on Sunday, November 15, after driving two of his luxury cars onto the sand at Diani Beach.

The vehicles in question were his signature yellow Lamborghini Urus and a grey Mercedes-Benz GLE. What started as a moment to show off the cars to friends at the Coast ended with both machines buried wheel-deep in the sand, unable to move.
"We drove onto the beach to show off, and now we are stuck," Kenyan Prince told his TikTok followers in footage he posted himself that evening.

In the clips, Kenyan Prince appeared shirtless in patterned swim shorts as he surveyed the situation.
The videos showed tyres spinning helplessly, flinging sand in all directions while the cars sank further with each attempt to accelerate.
He and his friend Mushkerr, along with others in their group, tried pushing the vehicles free but had no success. The spinning only deepened the holes beneath the wheels.

Pointing to the Lamborghini, he noted the suspension had lifted off the ground entirely. "The Lambo's suspension is even floating, clearly showing that it is in the air. It is tough. Anyway, pray for us," he said.

After inspecting the tyres and the underside of one of the cars, he raised concerns about the damage caused. "You see, the spade has even destroyed my car's tyres, and those tyres to replace are around Ksh400,000. And you can see there is even a scratch," he said.

He concluded that only specialised recovery equipment would do the job. "The only way that car has to be lifted is with a winch. That is the easiest way," he added.

The timing of the incident added an extra layer of irony. Just hours before the cars got stuck, Kenyan Prince had posted a YouTube video from Mombasa pushing back against claims that his Lamborghini had been repossessed by auctioneers after footage of a Lamborghini Urus on a vehicle carrier had circulated online.
"Now we are here. You can see the Lambo was brought here safely, and I wonder if people still believe that it had been auctioned," he said in that video.

The day before, on Saturday, November 14, he had already drawn attention at a Mombasa petrol station after accelerating the Lamborghini at high speed near a crowd, nearly knocking over a bystander who had to leap out of the way.
As of Monday morning, Kenyan Prince had not shared any update confirming whether the two cars had been successfully winched out or what the full extent of the damage turned out to be.
TikToker shows grave he bought at Lang'ata Cemetery during marriage breakup
Reactions online were largely amused, with many Kenyans treating the situation as a classic case of showing off gone wrong.
We also highlighted facts about Kenyan Prince’s challenge to Interpol and the US government, as the forex trader taunted officials from Dubai amid an international crackdown on alleged fraud.

At least 24 Kenyans have reportedly been arrested over a separate KSh 1.1 billion card fraud scheme, but authorities have not officially linked Omosa to the arrests. Despite the scrutiny, he told Interpol to “come for me here” and claimed he was “chilling in Dubai”.

Jinko Solar hosts Jinko Academy in Kenya to build local solar expertise
items.description: Jinko Solar held the Jinko Academy in Kenya with Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT) and the University of Nairobi. The
content: Jinko Solar, a global leader in photovoltaic technology and Battery Energy Storage Systems, has hosted the Jinko Academy in Kenya, bringing together academia and industry to strengthen local technical expertise in solar energy. The programme was delivered in collaboration with two of the country’s leading institutions, JKUAT and the University of Nairobi.

The Jinko Academy is designed to close the gap between theoretical learning and practical application in the renewable energy sector. Through its partnership with the two universities, Jinko Solar aims to equip students, researchers and local engineers with the skills needed to support Kenya’s growing solar industry and its Vision 2030 renewable energy goals.

The initiative comes at an important moment for Kenya’s energy landscape. Jinko Solar has a well established presence in the region. It supplied modules for the 50 MW Garissa solar plant and remains a leading module exporter to the Kenyan market. More recently, the company supplied its Tiger Neo 3.0 modules for Kenya’s largest private healthcare solar project, which covers more than 780 private hospitals nationwide.

During the academy sessions, participants worked directly with Jinko Solar’s technical experts on module manufacturing, system design and smart grid operations. The training also stressed practical applications, particularly in the high temperature and high irradiance conditions typical of Kenya, where reliable performance is critical.

The Jinko Academy reflects the company’s wider commitment to building capacity in emerging markets. As Kenya pursues an ambitious renewable energy agenda, partnerships between global technology leaders and local academic institutions are seen as essential to creating a skilled, self reliant workforce able to maintain and expand the country’s solar infrastructure.

Canada Announces Jobs for Kenyans and Other Foreigners, Lists 7 In-Demand Categories
items.description: Canada has announced employment opportunities for Kenyans and other foreign nationals, highlighting seven in-demand job categories facing labour shortages.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
TUKO.co.ke journalist Japhet Ruto has over eight years of experience in financial, business, and technology reporting, offering insights into Kenyan and global economic trends.

Canada has opened its doors to skilled workers from Kenya and other countries, with the country's immigration authority identifying seven occupational categories where it urgently needs talent to plug gaps in its labour market.

The Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) made the announcement on Monday, November 16, through its official account on X, calling on experienced professionals abroad to consider joining the Canadian workforce.

PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
The seven categories listed under Canada's Express Entry system cover a broad range of professions.
Medical doctors, researchers, and senior managers who already have Canadian work experience are among those being targeted, alongside health care and social services professionals.
The IRCC also indicated it is actively seeking tradespeople and educators, as well as professionals working in science , technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields.

Transport sector professionals form another priority group, while workers with French-language proficiency round out the seven categories, reflecting Canada's sustained effort to maintain and grow its bilingual character.

Express Entry is Canada's flagship points-based immigration system, designed to fast-track the selection of skilled foreign nationals for permanent residency. Candidates are assessed on factors including age, education, work experience, and language skills, with higher-scoring profiles receiving invitations to apply for permanent residence.

The latest category-based selection rounds signal that Canada is not only looking to manage general immigration volumes but is specifically targeting professionals whose skills align with current economic needs.

For Kenyan professionals in health care, engineering, education, or the trades, the announcement represents a direct recruitment signal from one of the world's most sought-after immigration destinations.
In other news, Canada’s Rural Community Immigration Programme offers skilled workers and international graduates a pathway to permanent residency through employment in rural communities.
The programme was made permanent, giving participating communities a long-term way to attract foreign workers and address labour shortages.
It also creates opportunities for eligible newcomers seeking to settle and work in smaller Canadian communities.

items.title: Turkana moves to strengthen healthcare under BREHS project
items.description: Ministry of Health in collaboration with the World Bank and Turkana County Government has undertaken a five-day Implementation Support Mission for the Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems (BREHS) Project.
content: Ministry of Health in collaboration with the World Bank and Turkana County Government has undertaken a five-day Implementation Support Mission for the Building Resilient and Responsive Health Systems (BREHS) Project.

The mission seeks to assess county preparedness, strengthen coordination among implementing partners and agree on priority actions to support effective project implementation, which aims to improve healthcare delivery for refugees and host communities.

According to a statement, the key areas include workforce and infrastructure readiness, risk management, implementation planning, financing and alignment with the Shirika Plan to improve healthcare delivery for refugees and host communities.
Turkana is among 45 counties that have met BREHS compliance requirements and qualified for the first tranche of project funding.

BREHS is a five-year initiative aimed at strengthening resilient health systems and expanding access to quality primary healthcare, particularly maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health services.
The Ministry remains committed to supporting county-led implementation, strengthening partnerships and ensuring equitable access to quality healthcare for all.

The Ministry’s delegation, led by BREHS Project Lead Dr Terry Kamau, was received by Turkana County CECM for Health and Sanitation Services Dr Epem Joseph, alongside Chief Officer for Medical Services Dr Gilchrist Lokoel and Chief Officer for Preventive and Promotive Health Services Agnes Mana.
The engagement brings together representatives from the Council of Governors, Public Service Commission, Kenya Medical Training College, County Health Management Team and other implementing partners.

The mission includes field assessments at Kakuma Health Facility and the proposed Lodwar blood service site, alongside discussions on KMTC sponsorship, infrastructure development, recruitment of technical personnel and resource utilisation.

World Bank Health Economist Paul Bartilol emphasised the need to begin preparations for FY2028 planning within the next three months to ensure county priorities are reflected in future funding allocations.
The mission will conclude with engagements involving the Governor and county leadership to review findings, agree on implementation milestones and strengthen county ownership.

items.title: County pledges staff, equipment for Saos Dispensary as it accelerates SHA drive
items.description: County pledges staff, equipment for Saos Dispensary as it accelerates SHA drive Kenya News Agency
content: Uasin Gishu County Chief Officer for Preventive and Promotive Health Services Dr Billy Lubanga on Monday visited Saos Dispensary in Ziwa Ward, Soy Sub-County, assuring residents of stronger services through extra staff, laboratory equipment and expanded care, while urging full uptake of the Social Health Authority (SHA) cover.
Standing at the facility, Dr Lubanga told staff and community members:

“We are committed to improving healthcare delivery here. Additional staff will be deployed and laboratory equipment provided to enhance diagnostic services so that patients get better care closer to home.”
He stressed the critical role of SHA registration.

“Register with the Social Health Authority. This cover enables you to access healthcare services beyond dispensaries to higher-level health facilities when necessary. It is the pathway to quality care without the fear of catastrophic costs.”
Lubanga also highlighted the Facility Improvement Fund (FIF) as a key tool for expanding and upgrading facilities.
He noted that local graduates holding health-related qualifications would be considered for jobs as Saos Dispensary grows.
The official further called on Community Health Promoters (CHPs) to remain “the eyes of the Health Department in the community” by strengthening service delivery and linking residents to care.
The Chief Officer reaffirmed his commitment to the facility’s continued growth and paid tribute to Governor Dr Jonathan Bii Chelilim for sustained investment in the county’s health sector.
Saos Facility In-Charge Bethwel Kurgat welcomed the visit. “We appreciate the department’s commitment to addressing the facility’s needs,” he said.

“Additional staff, laboratory equipment and improved access to SHA services will go a long way in enhancing service delivery, reducing the challenges faced by patients and ensuring the community receives quality healthcare closer to home,” remarked Kurgat.
The visit comes as Uasin Gishu intensifies efforts to enrol residents under SHA, the national scheme designed to deliver universal health coverage.

The County latest data have shown registration figures rising steadily, with more than 515,000 residents enrolled at one recent count (around 44–45 per cent coverage), while over 200 health facilities across the county have been onboarded.
Nationally, enrolment has surpassed 26 million and continues to climb toward broader targets.
It is important to note that SHA enables free or heavily subsidized services at primary facilities and seamless referral to higher-level care, protecting households from the high cost of treatment.

The County leadership has repeatedly urged registration through facility desks, CHPs and the *147# USSD code, with special support for the elderly, persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups under Governor Bii’s administration.

Officials say the combination of stronger local facilities like Saos Dispensary and widespread SHA uptake is central to bringing reliable, affordable healthcare within reach of every household in Ziwa Ward and beyond.

items.title: Only 19pc of Kenyan women have ever been screened for cervical cancer – survey
items.description: As the world marks Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, a new survey shows that only 19 per cent of Kenyan women aged 15-49 have ever been screened for the disease.
content: As the world marks Cervical Cancer Elimination Day, a new survey shows that only 19 per cent of Kenyan women aged 15-49 have ever been screened for the disease.

As the world marks Cervical Cancer Elimination Day on November 17, a new survey has revealed that only 19 per cent of Kenyan women aged 15-49 have ever been tested for the disease, exposing gaps in access to early detection across the country.

The 2025/2026 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS) by the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) shows that women in urban areas are more likely to have been screened (21 per cent) than their rural counterparts (17 per cent).

The gaps are more pronounced across some counties, with Tana River, Garissa and West Pokot recording the lowest screening levels at 3 per cent each, followed by Wajir at 1 per cent and Mandera at less than 1 per cent.

The survey also shows that 59 per cent of women aged 15-19 have received at least one dose of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, which protects against the virus strains responsible for most cervical cancer cases.
However, vaccination coverage varies considerably across counties, standing at 88 per cent in Kitui, 83 per cent in Kilifi, 81 per cent in Vihiga and 80 per cent in Kericho.
Mandera recorded the lowest coverage at just 1 per cent, followed by Garissa at 8 per cent and Wajir at 9 per cent.
The survey further indicates that HPV vaccination coverage declines with age, from 75 per cent among 15-year-olds to 35 per cent among 19-year-olds.
“Overall, 59% of women age 15-19 have received at least one dose of the HPV vaccine, and 48% have ever received an HPV vaccination card,” the survey reveals.

School-based immunisation accounts for the largest share of HPV vaccinations, with 86 per cent of vaccinated women aged 15-49 receiving their most recent dose at school, while 12 per cent received it at a public health facility.

The findings come as the World Health Organisation (WHO) renews its call for stronger political commitment, sustained investment and equitable access to cervical cancer prevention, screening and treatment.

WHO says eliminating cervical cancer by 2030 will require countries to meet the 90-70-90 targets, which include vaccinating 90 per cent of girls against HPV by age 15, screening 70 per cent of women using a high-performance test by ages 35 and 45, and ensuring 90 per cent of women diagnosed with cervical disease receive appropriate treatment.
